findings.scenario: Any window resize (including mobile browser chrome show/hide) debounces into cleanup()+full remount. Load/timeline-load tweens replay from their FROM state, ScrollTriggers are recreated, and in-memory replay==='once' flags/listeners are reset, so once animations can play again and rest-state elements jump.
findings.remediation: Do not remount on raw resize. Subscribe to breakpoint and prefers-reduced-motion MediaQueryList change events and re-apply only when that signature changes; keep once-played ids across breakpoint-stable refreshes.

findings.scenario: Script runs before window.gsap or window.ScrollTrigger exist, or ScrollTrigger is absent. Valid hover/exit/load/entrance entries are dropped with no retry and no no-motion fallback. Motion stays dead until something else calls rehydrate (resize is the only automatic path).
findings.remediation: Apply non-scroll kinds when only gsap is present; queue/retry rehydrate until both libs exist or emit a hard failure; do not silently return after cleanup.

findings.scenario: prefers-reduced-motion is sampled only inside applyManifest. Toggling the OS setting after load leaves JS tweens running (or no-motion stuck) until a remount. destroy() also classList.remove('no-motion'), so teardown re-enables CSS motion for reduced-motion users.
findings.remediation: Bind matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') change to rehydrate; on reduce, cleanup and keep html.no-motion; never strip that class while the MQ still matches, including in destroy().

findings.scenario: preview() ignores state.destroyed, always applyManifest({entries:[entry]}) (wiping the live manifest), then returns true whenever the node exists and gsap exists—even if install skipped (reduced motion, breakpoint miss, canvas/iframe, missing ScrollTrigger). Callers treat preview as played; a later resize rehydrate restores __ONEBOX_MOTION_MANIFEST__ only if that timer was not cleared by cleanup.
findings.remediation: No-op preview when destroyed or when install will not attach; return false unless the matching tween/listener actually started; preview into a child context instead of replacing the full manifest.

findings.scenario: entries are not required to have unique id values. Two viewport/scroll/timeline-viewport items with the same UUID register the same ScrollTrigger id; the second registration collides and the first trigger/animation is killed or overwritten.
findings.remediation: Reject manifests whose entry.id (and, for a given timelineId, conflicting trigger/replay tuples) are not unique before install.

audit.proof_assessment: No proof artifacts were supplied. Coverage of IMP-066-073 was judged only from templates/local-service/motion-runtime.js; nothing demonstrates replay, reduced-motion, breakpoint, cleanup, or timeline behavior under the failing states above.
residual_risks: load/manual timeline replay==='repeat' has no repeat signal beyond remount
scroll scrub:true ignores toggleActions, so replay once/repeat is not honored
equal timeline order values still chain sequentially rather than overlapping
no MutationObserver; swapped [data-edit-id] nodes stay inert until an external rehydrate
without matchMedia, every named breakpoint matches at once and can stack tweens on one node
